summary: An active second-year Q School card does not preserve access to main-tour qualifiers when the two-year World Ranking falls below 128.
evidence: A seven-season instrumented replay exactly matched all seven original season reports. On 2032-08-16 the player was #134 with hasTourCard=true, currentYear=2, yearsRemaining=1 and expiry 2032/33. English, International, UK, Welsh, World Open and World Championship qualifying were blocked across 37 recorded snapshots. Card loss was not recorded until 2033-06-30.
impact: The player can lose a protected season of main-tour opportunities, weakening retention and promotion balance. This is distinct from legitimate card expiry.

summary: Age 49 has no valid starting career route
evidence: The catalogue allows Bottom Tour only through age 48 and Masters from age 50; every other route ends earlier. getEligibleStartingLevels returns an empty list at 49. getValidatedStartingLevel then returns the first catalogue entry, start-club-junior, despite its age limit of 16. NewCareerPage does not disable Start Career for this condition. The age-49 matrix cases exercise this fallback and must not be treated as valid senior starts. The completed fallback careers recorded only 1 win in 105 matches and 1 in 104.
impact: Provide a valid age-49 route and stop invalid fallback configurations being silently accepted. The requested Masters route also legitimately resolves to Top 64 at 45 and Bottom Tour at 46–48; those actual routes are recorded in the CSV.

summary: The youngest starting path still produces long runs of defeats despite eventual career progression.
evidence: Seed 104729 recorded 14 wins in 142 matches from starting ages 12 through 17, including 0-23 at age 15. Seed 130363 recorded 25 wins in 137 matches in those years. Both ultimately earned professional cards and finished positive.
impact: Financial survival and eventual promotion do not establish that the first several seasons are enjoyable. The automated manager may select events that are too difficult.

summary: Late starting careers stay solvent but provide very few wins or trophies under the automated manager.
evidence: The age-40 starts finished 49/207 and 47/226 for wins/matches; the age-50 starts finished 11/106 and 7/103. None of these four careers won a recorded singles title. All reached 65 with positive balances.
impact: A career can remain technically playable while offering an unrewarding experience. Inspect accessible local/seniors competition strength and manager event selection before changing match fairness.

summary: Large savings still accumulate when the automated manager keeps ongoing costs very low.
evidence: Over 48 seasons this career earned £5,968,259 prize money and £4,598,369 sponsor income, ending with £10,042,702. Recorded staff costs totalled £93,913 and facility costs were zero. Sponsorship fell from £106,894 in the age-49 season to £27,837 at 51 and £9,500 at 60; pre-existing signed contracts are honoured.
impact: Cash remains positive and sponsorship falls after card loss, but elite-player spending may stop being meaningful. These are recorded audit categories and are not a complete reconciliation (see the separate finance-reporting defect). The audit manager chooses cheap staff and free facilities; review realistic management policies and optional costs before adding compulsory cash drains.

summary: The audit emits two warnings for the same World Championship win-rate statistic.
evidence: Both warnings describe a 61.9% win rate in 42 main-draw matches with no World title. The career lost its World finals; this is possible and is not itself a game bug.
impact: Count this as one heuristic concern, not two game defects. Raw warning rows remain available for transparency.

summary: Human world-player records count events as matches
evidence: advanceWorldPlayersForNewSeason builds seasonRecord.matches from event counts while its wins/losses count matches; the evidence-based correction explicitly excludes the human. In age50 seed104729, the canonical first-season report correctly records 7 matches (3 wins, 4 losses), while the human world-player copy records 4 matches with the same 3 wins and 4 losses. Annual copies accumulate the mismatch. CPU rows pass this specific check.
impact: The human profile headline uses careerLegacyOf and is protected, but playerSeasonHistory prefers the incorrect saved seasonal match count, so the human profile season table can be inconsistent. Repair the duplicate human world record and its old seasonal totals. This finding does not establish incorrect ranking credits; ranking awards use the result ledger.

summary: Audit finance categories do not fully reconcile to actual cash movement
evidence: The age12 seed104729 first season changes cash by -£6,758.50, while audit categories sum to -£7,299.50: a £541 residual. Two instrumented replays exactly matched the original season report. £450 net team-event fees/awards plus £91 withdrawal refunds fully explain that residual. Both kinds of action change cash without updating the audit categories. Final cash comes directly from the save, not the category sum.
impact: Treat the detailed category breakdown as incomplete. The reproduced discrepancy is in audit accounting, not money being created or lost in the game. Capture every action cash delta and separately classify team rewards, costs and refunds.
